Plan a charging site

Every property has its own reason to charge.

A guest stopping overnight, an employee parking all day and a resident returning home each need a different service. The site, power supply and way people park determine the design.

Hotels & destinations

Make charging part of a good arrival.

Guests should be able to find a bay, start a charge and get on with their stay. We position the chargers around the arrival route and choose a charging speed that suits the time people actually spend on site.

For the driver
Clear bays, straightforward payment and a dependable overnight charge.

For the property
Control over guest access and pricing, usage reports and support when something stops working.

See West Pier House

Workplaces

Use the hours people are already parked.

A working day gives vehicles time to charge without demanding a high-power unit in every space. We map staff and visitor use, then share the available electrical capacity across the bays.

For the driver
Reliable access during the working day, with no need to detour to a public charging hub.

For the property
Managed load, access rules and a route to add bays as the number of EV drivers grows.

See Northline Yard

Residential developments

Make home charging possible for more residents.

Shared parking works best with one coordinated electrical plan. We bring the first bays online, give each resident their own access and energy record, and prepare the distribution for later phases.

For the driver
Convenient overnight charging and a clear bill for their own use.

For the property
One managed system and a fair process for expanding beyond the first group of bays.

See Greyfriars House

For property owners & operators

Have a place where charging could work?

Tell us about the parking, the power and the people who use it. We’ll help shape a practical first phase and a plan for what follows.
